title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
abstract: arXiv:2608.23858v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), introduced by Google, enables large language model (LLM)-driven shopping agents to authorize and execute payments on behalf of users. Its signed Checkout and Payment Mandates protect the integrity of transaction data after signing. Agent interactions and external inputs that shape a transaction before authorization remain outside that protection, including Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A) messages and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls. Prior work identified replay and prompt-injection attacks in AP2 v0.1. AP2 v0.2 addresses some of these issues but adds capabilities and deployment assumptions that require renewed analysis. We present a systematic security analysis of AP2 v0.2 based on its roles, transaction lifecycle, deployment architectures, and trust boundaries. translated_title: 超越授权：代理支付协议（AP2）的系统性安全分析
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23858v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：由谷歌推出的代理支付协议（AP2）使大型语言模型（LLM）驱动的购物代理能够代表用户授权并执行支付。其签署的结账和支付授权保护了签署后交易数据的完整性。然而，在授权前塑造交易的代理交互和外部输入（包括代理间协议（A2A）消息和模型上下文协议（MCP）工具调用）不受此保护。先前的研究已识别出AP2 v0.1中的重放和提示注入攻击。AP2 v0.2解决了其中一些问题，但增加了需要重新分析的功能和部署假设。我们基于其角色、交易生命周期、部署架构和信任边界，对AP2 v0.2进行了系统性安全分析。我们将生命周期划分为五个阶段，并识别出五种部署架构。利用MAESTRO（多代理环境、安全、...）
tldr: 本文对谷歌AP2 v0.2协议进行了系统性安全分析，通过划分交易生命周期和部署架构，揭示了在授权前外部输入环节存在的安全漏洞。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a systematic security analysis of Google's AP2 v0.2 protocol, identifying vulnerabilities in pre-authorization external inputs by segmenting transaction lifecycle and deployment architectures.
